run.notes: First light and full sweep. Context x output-length at concurrency 1, plus TWO concurrency sweeps at a fixed 512/128 shape. Prompt cache defeated by --prompt-mode shuffled: Ollama drops cache_prompt in its OpenAI translation, so the sibling's method does not work here. A FIRST context run was discarded because Ollama spells the reasoning delta `reasoning` rather than llama.cpp's `reasoning_content`, so the harness stamped zero tokens in all ten cells; kept beside this one as sweep.DISCARDED-zero-decode.json. The concurrency sweep was run twice because the first configuration did not fit -- see the two workload notes.

hardware.accelerator: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 Ti with Max-Q Design

host.notes: TU117, compute capability 7.5, NO tensor cores -- not comparable to the T4-based g4dn/g5g rigs at equal compute capability. Max-Q: thermally throttled. Driver 610.57.04, reported to Ollama as CUDA 13.3.

model.architecture_notes: An OLLAMA TAG, not a Hub id: Google's QAT Q4_0 GGUF re-containered with the embedded chat template stripped (model blob 3,349,514,112 B vs Google's 3,349,516,256; digests differ). Reasoning model -- content_chunks is 0 and reasoning_chunks is the whole stream in every cell here, so at 32 and 128 output tokens every cell measures the thinking phase and no cell completed a task. The tag also bundles a 986 MB vision+audio projector that the daemon loads unconditionally.

software.notes: Ollama links llama.cpp and starts a llama-server child; the child's own flags are the daemon's choices, not ours: --mmproj (unconditional), --no-jinja --chat-template chatml (the GGUF template is replaced by Ollama's Go renderer, renderer=gemma4 parser=gemma4), --flash-attn auto, -b 512 -ub 512, --context-shift --keep 4.

memory.notes: MEASURED 2762 MiB of 4096 at 8192 context, against local-llamacpp-1650ti-2b-q4_0's 1618 MiB for the same weights. Breakdown from the daemon log: 1341.78 model buffer + 48.00 KV non-SWA (8192 cells x 3 layers) + 12.00 KV SWA (1024 cells x 12 layers) + 122.52 compute buffer + 1154.07 mmproj + ~84 CUDA context. `ollama ps` reports 1.7 GB -- it does not count the projector, so it must not be used to size this rig. NOTE the SWA cache is capped at its 1024-cell window regardless of n_ctx, so KV is 60 MiB where MODELS.md's 18 KiB/token predicts 144.

workload.tool: sweep.py (copy of local-llamacpp-1650ti-2b-q4_0's, three further bugs fixed)
workload.notes: decode-source auto -> stream; Ollama emits no usage.decode_tokens_per_second and no Prometheus endpoint, so metrics.prom is empty. The sweep array holds three groups: concurrency 1 points whose input_len varies are the CONTEXT sweep (OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=8192 NUM_PARALLEL=1); the 512/128 points are the CONCURRENCY sweep at NUM_PARALLEL=8, which is the configuration that FITS this card; the concurrency points marked degraded were run at NUM_PARALLEL=32 and did not fit.

issues.summary: Ollama's OpenAI stream spells the reasoning delta `reasoning`, not llama.cpp's `reasoning_content`, and pairs it with an empty-string `content`. A harness reading only the llama.cpp field name records zero tokens in every cell.

cache_prompt:false does not survive Ollama's OpenAI-to-native translation, so the prefix cache cannot be defeated the way the sibling defeats it. Measured: an 8-token request carrying the flag still logged cached n_tokens = 660 of 661.
Ollama's prompt cache outlives the client, so a deterministically seeded prompt generator makes a second process hit the first one's cache -- 0.15 s against 2.17 s cold on a 652-token prompt.

OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH is multiplied by OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL (llama.cpp DIVIDES its -c across slots), and a MULTIMODAL model additionally gets a 2048-token minimum per slot. MEASURED across four settings: the stock tag took 1024->2048 and 1536->2048 while the projector-free variant honoured 1024, 1536 and 8192 exactly. That floor is why this run could not reach the sibling's geometry; 2026-09-04-text-only-ollama-1650ti does.

Partial offload is silent. At NUM_PARALLEL=32 the daemon offloaded 26/36 layers and put 512 MiB of KV on the host; nothing raised an error and `ollama ps` said 60%/40% CPU/GPU only if you looked. No configuration knob prevents it -- dropping the projector does.
At num_predict=128 on /api/generate, both `response` and `thinking` come back EMPTY with done_reason 'length' -- 128 tokens generated, zero characters returned.

notes: Paired with local-llamacpp-1650ti-2b-q4_0's 2026-09-03-full-sweep-1650ti: same card, same weights, same engine, different daemon. End-to-end ties within 1% in all ten context cells; corrected decode is ~3% behind; VRAM is +1144 MiB for a projector this workload never touches.

TTFT tracks the sibling within 5% at every concurrency level and doubles exactly with each doubling of c on both rigs -- prefill does not batch on either runtime, and aggregate output saturates near 46 tok/s here against 45-48 there.
The concurrency c=2 cell is NOT a result: 23.7% spread across three repeats, against <=0.5% in every other cell. This part is Max-Q and throttles; never read a single row.

The c=4 gap (35.17 vs the sibling's 45.12) is real at 0.4% spread and is NOT isolated: the two servers do not have the same slot geometry (2048 tokens/slot here, 1024 there, because this daemon will not accept 1024), so scheduler behaviour and slot size are confounded.
Ollama serves no Prometheus endpoint -- GET /metrics returns 404 -- so metrics.prom is empty in both runs. llama-server has one. This is not a harness failure.
The two rigs defeated the prompt cache by DIFFERENT means, both verified to cached=0: the sibling by cache_prompt:false, this rig by --prompt-mode shuffled.
Not comparable to the T4-based g4dn/g5g rigs at equal compute capability 7.5: TU117 has no tensor cores, TU104 does.
